consensus_summary: Consensus treats butter/curds primarily as a symbol of abundance, prosperity, richness, and divine material provision (often with honey/oil/milk), while noting context-dependent alternatives: subsistence after desolation (Isa 7), flattering/smooth speech (Ps 55:21), the product of churning/pressure (Prov 30:33), hospitality, and occasional patristic links to Christ’s humanity or doctrinal richness. No settled single meaning.
book_summary: Butter is the word worked from milk into sound judgment—teaching tested until one can refuse evil and choose good; worked into the walk it cleanses the feet; its counterfeit is smooth speech concealing war.
consensus_core_identification: Abundance, prosperity, and rich divine provision (pastoral fatness of the land).
book_core_identification: Matured/tested teaching (the word worked from milk) that yields sound moral judgment, with an applied sense of cleansing one’s walk and a counterfeit of hypocritical flattery.
boundary_disagreement: Consensus centers cases of plenty, desolation-diet, hospitality, and occasional process or speech metaphors; the book re-centers on a spiritual product of ‘working’ the word into discernment and foot-cleansing, treating smooth speech only as counterfeit rather than a parallel sense of the same symbol, and does not treat abundance/subsistence as the symbol’s identity.
material_contradiction: Consensus primary identification (butter = abundance/rich provision) and the book’s identification (butter = tested word/sound judgment that refuses evil and chooses good) cannot both be the core referent in the same sense; accepting the book replaces the consensus core rather than narrowing it.
rationale: Reduced cores differ in kind: material/providential richness versus a processed spiritual result (worked milk → discernment), with Job 29:6/John 13 supplying a walk-cleansing extension absent from consensus. Shared verses (Prov 30:33 process; Isa 7:15 purpose clause; Ps 55:21 flattery) are reused but reassigned—Isa 7’s diet becomes the judgment itself, not food marking abundance or scarcity—so the book rejects rather than refines the consensus referent. Minority ‘doctrinal richness’ notes are too thin and non-equivalent to cover the book’s specific core.
strongest_objection: Standard interpretation reads Isa 7:15/22 as diet (abundance or subsistence), not as butter literally being sound judgment; linking Job 29:6’s ‘washed…with butter’ to John 13 foot-washing is analogical and extra-textual, so the synthesis may be idiosyncratic allegory rather than the passages’ sense.
